input:
## Basis

The column is intended to separate a liquid feed at a design throughput of 7 t per day, with a separation duty under which 95% of the key component is to be taken overhead. All wetted parts are specified in 316L stainless steel, a point which is stated here once and is not repeated in the sections that follow. The feed is taken as characterised at the battery limit: its composition and condition are those of the upstream unit under its normal operation, and the design does not make provision for feed cases lying beyond the normal range. The product specifications comprise the overhead purity implied by the duty, together with a bottoms stream that is fit to pass on to the next unit. Utilities are assumed to be available at the site conditions, and the column is designed for continuous operation at the stated throughput, with the question of turndown left open at this stage and carried forward into the risks section. The design pressure and temperature, it should be noted, follow the relief case of the upstream unit together with the heating medium of the reboiler, and the shell is rated for the coincident case rather than for the normal operating point.

## Sizing

The diameter of the column is set by the vapour load at the top of the column, where the vapour rate is at its highest and the allowable velocity fixes the cross-sectional area required. The internals are chosen with a liquid feed of this size in mind: trays offer a robust separation with a predictable pressure drop and tolerate the solids and fouling tendency of a plant stream, whereas packing would offer a lower pressure drop in a taller, narrower shell, and is accordingly set aside on fouling grounds rather than on separation grounds. The height follows from the number of contacting stages that the separation duty requires at the chosen reflux, together with the disengaging and sump allowances at the two ends. It is worth noting that the reflux is set by the duty: the specified removal fixes the split, and the reflux ratio is the operating variable that delivers it, so that the sizing and the energy balance amount to one single calculation rather than two separate ones. The reboiler and the condenser are sized along with the column, on the basis of the vapour and liquid rates that the balance returns.

## Materials

The stainless steel specified in the basis is used for the shell, for the internals, and for the wetted parts of the nozzles and instruments. The grade has been chosen with the corrosion duty of the feed and the products at the column temperatures in mind: the feed is aqueous in character and carries chlorides at levels which rule out carbon steel for wetted service, and the grade specified resists that attack over the design life with the usual corrosion allowance duly applied. Gaskets and bolting follow the same duty, with the gasket materials matched to the process fluid and to the flange temperatures rather than to the shell. Carbon steel is confined to the skirt, to the platforms, and to the external supports, where the process fluid cannot reach it. No lining or cladding is proposed: the solid grade represents the simpler construction at this diameter, and it conveniently leaves the internal surfaces available for inspection.

## Risks

Fouling constitutes the first open item. The feed carries the fouling tendency that is recorded in the basis, and the design does not settle how rapidly deposits will form on the trays and in the reboiler, nor what effect they will have on the pressure drop and on the separation over the course of a run. The choice of internals reduces the exposure but does not remove it altogether, and no cleaning interval can responsibly be stated until such time as fouling data on this particular feed exist.

Turndown constitutes the second open item. The column has been designed at the stated throughput, and its behaviour at reduced rates has not been established: trays weep and packing maldistributes as rates fall, and the reflux that delivers the duty at the design rate may well fail to deliver it at the lowest rate that the plant will ask for. Neither item is resolved in this report. Fouling is carried as an allowance in the pressure drop and in the reboiler margin, and turndown as an operating limit still to be confirmed, and both are set out here so that the design is read with its open items duly attached.

Stage efficiency is taken at the value the internals vendor quotes for this class of separation, and the actual stage count is the theoretical count divided by that efficiency. The margin between the two counts is the sizing's allowance for the internals performing below their test behaviour in plant service, where distribution is poorer and the feed arrives with the plant's fluctuations on it. The reflux drum, the feed preheat, and the control valves on the product lines are sized in the same pass, on the rates the balance returns at the design point, so that the column and its immediate auxiliaries rest on one set of rates.

## Materials

The stainless steel specified in the basis is used for the shell, the internals, and the wetted parts of the nozzles and instruments. No lining or cladding is proposed: the solid grade is the simpler construction at this diameter, and it leaves the internal surfaces inspectable. Inspection follows the same division as the materials choice: wetted surfaces are examined for pitting and crevice attack at the tray attachments and at the liquid lines, where the chloride duty concentrates, and the examination interval is set by the corrosion allowance consumed at the rate the first examinations measure.

## Risks

Fouling is the first open item. The feed carries the fouling tendency recorded in the basis, and the design does not settle how fast deposits will form on the trays and in the reboiler, nor what they will do to the pressure drop and the separation over a run. The internals choice reduces the exposure but does not remove it, and a cleaning interval cannot be stated until fouling data on this feed exist. The allowance stands in place of data, and the pressure-drop trend over the first period of operation is the evidence that will show whether it was set generously or tightly.

Turndown is the second open item. The column is designed at the stated throughput, and its behaviour at reduced rates is not established: trays weep and packing maldistribute as rates fall, and the reflux that delivers the duty at design rate may not deliver it at the lowest rate the plant will ask for. A minimum operating rate, once confirmed, binds the plant as well as the column, since the units upstream and downstream must turn down with it. Neither item is resolved in this report. Fouling is carried as an allowance in the pressure drop and the reboiler margin, turndown as an operating limit to be confirmed, and both are stated here so that the design is read with its open items attached.
